whisper: A flower once cost more than a house. Holland. The sixteen thirties. Everyone wanted tulips. The rarest ones had wild flame stripes caused by a virus. People traded bulbs still in the ground on paper in taverns. One bulb reportedly sold for ten thousand guilders. A craftsman made about three hundred a year. Then, in February sixteen thirty seven, the market crashed. But a historian who checked the records couldn't find anyone who went bankrupt.
